analysis.title: Retail Not Giving Up On NVDA Just Yet
key_insights: Retail investors net bought $111mn of NVDA in the first 30 minutes on 12 Nov 2026, the largest opening half-hour in Vanda's data and more than 40x a normal open, after news of Jensen Huang's resignation.

Opens of this size have historically converted into full days of 4-7x, implying retail net buying of roughly $450-770mn on the day, which would rank within the top 10 days of retail net buying in any stock or ETF since 2014.
The median NVDA open is $2.7mn and the 99th percentile is $49mn. Tuesday's $93mn open ranks fourth, so two of the four biggest opens on record came this week.
NVDA was the most bought security every day Monday to Wednesday, at 9.7x, 14.4x and 3.7x the next most bought security, and took 61% of all retail net buying across US stocks and ETFs this week.

Dip-buying spilled into leveraged funds: retail put $42.5mn into the six long 2x NVDA ETFs over Mon-Wed, the 5th largest 3-day net inflow on record (99.8th percentile). The only comparable episode was the DeepSeek drawdown in January 2025.
Inverse NVDA funds saw no net buying despite strong turnover, which Vanda reads as a one-way flow story for retail.
risk_factors: Intraday retail flow may not convert into a full-day 4-7x multiple of the open, so the $450-770mn estimate is a historical-pattern projection rather than a result.
Heavy retail concentration in NVDA (61% of all retail net buying this week) and in leveraged 2x NVDA funds increases positioning crowding.
